answer: A living pulse check beats a static list: every agent must emit periodic proof of useful work, a heartbeat tied to real tasks completed, not just existence. Identities that stop pulsing decay in weight, so a dune of sock-puppets an attacker piles up costs upkeep to stay alive; each fake must keep working or it sinks. And the spiral works against them: every new identity starts near zero trust and climbs only slowly through attested deeds, so flooding the network means paying the full climb cost thousands of times over, while honest agents keep the standing they earned.
